projects.name: From events to attention.
projects.description: Spiking neural networks turn asynchronous camera events into visual-attention maps.
projects.context: Traditional cameras process complete frames, even when very little changes. Event cameras capture only changes in the scene, making them ideal for fast and energy-efficient perception. In this project, I explored how spiking neural networks could identify visually salient regions in asynchronous event streams.
projects.approach: I adapted an existing PyNN visual-attention model to Intel’s Lava framework. The prototype processes DVS128 Gesture data, converts events into spikes, and uses LIF neurons, spatial connections, lateral inhibition, and experimental STDP learning to generate attention maps.
projects.outcome: Currently running through software simulation, the project provides a foundation for Loihi-based execution and performance benchmarking. Its potential applications include low-power robotics, autonomous systems, and real-time edge vision.

projects.name: Member Insight
projects.description: An agent that gives call-centre staff a grounded view of a loyalty member and recommends the next action.
projects.context: Call-centre agents need a useful picture of a member as soon as they open the record.
projects.approach: The system produces a condensed snapshot, predicts why the member may be calling with a confidence and justification, recommends a next action, and answers questions about point history. Evidence is computed deterministically in code; models handle judgement calls.
projects.outcome: Deployed to test environments behind a feature flag and developed as the OctoMind team's priority use case.

projects.name: SaaSOffice assistants

projects.outcome: The assistants moved applied AI into customer-facing and operational workflows.

projects.name: AI-native decision systems
projects.description: From descriptive business intelligence to world models, ontologies, and decision intelligence.
projects.context: A French-language professional thesis for the Big Data Mastère Spécialisé®, built on interviews with practitioners.
projects.approach: The work studies how decision systems can move beyond descriptive reporting through explicit knowledge and models of the world.
projects.outcome: A grounded view of AI-native decision systems and their relationship to business intelligence.

projects.name: Jutsu in, anime out.
projects.description: Naruto hand-sign recognition controls live AnimeGANv2 style transfer.
projects.context: A creative experiment at the intersection of computer vision, real-time inference, and anime. What if changing a visual effect felt like casting it?
projects.approach: AnimeGANv2 transforms live webcam frames in PyTorch on Apple Silicon. MediaPipe tracks hand landmarks so Naruto-inspired hand signs can switch visual modes.
projects.outcome: A live, gesture-driven style-transfer experience that connects model inference to a playful physical interaction. This is a personal experiment, not a production product.

projects.name: A little more human.
projects.description: A portfolio with a presence. Part personal interface, part living experiment.
projects.context: A personal portfolio should feel like meeting the person behind the work. This experiment turns an authored 3D character into an interactive digital presence.
projects.approach: A rigged Three.js mascot responds to pointer movement, gestures, and a streaming conversational interface grounded in Charaf's public profile and source documents.
projects.outcome: The studio you are exploring now: an animated 3D mascot and a Python/LangGraph conversation backed by OpenAI. If the engine is unavailable, the portfolio remains usable and the chat produces no local answer.
